# How to use Claude Projects to keep your work organised

**Hook:** By the end of this guide you’ll be able to create a Claude Project, drop in related conversations and files, and view everything in one tidy place – perfect for anyone who needs a clear, goal‑focused workspace.

## Before you start
- You have an active Anthropic (Claude) account.  
- You can access the Claude web‑app on a desktop or laptop.  
- You’ve got at least one chat or a document you want to group together.

## Step 1 — Open the Claude dashboard
Head to the Claude home page and sign in. Look for the **“Dashboard”** button at the top‑right of the screen – it usually looks like a grid of squares. This area is the hub where all your conversations, projects and files live.  
💬 **Example:** Click the button that says *Dashboard* (or a similar icon) to land on a page that lists your recent chats.

## Step 2 — Create a new Project
On the Dashboard, find the **“New Project”** button – often a plus sign next to the word *Projects*. Click it, then give your project a clear name that reflects the goal you’re working towards, such as *“Q3 Marketing Campaign”*. Adding a short description helps teammates understand the purpose later.  
💬 **Example:** Enter `Q3 Marketing Campaign` as the title and `All copy, ad ideas and feedback for the upcoming quarter` as the description, then hit *Create*.

## Step 3 — Add existing chats to the Project
Inside your new Project, look for an **“Add conversation”** option (usually a button with a chat bubble icon). Click it, then browse the list of recent chats or search by keyword. Select the conversations that relate to your project and confirm. This pulls the whole dialogue into the project, keeping the context together.  
💬 **Example:** Tick the boxes next to chats named *“Ad copy brainstorming”* and *“Email subject line ideas”*, then press *Add*.

## Step 4 — Attach files or documents
Projects can hold more than just chats. Find the **“Attach file”** button – often a paper‑clip icon – and upload any relevant PDFs, spreadsheets or images. Once uploaded, you’ll see a thumbnail preview inside the project view.  
💬 **Example:** Drag your `CampaignBrief.pdf` into the upload area, or click *Browse* and select the file from your computer.

## Step 5 — Use project‑wide prompts
With everything gathered, you can ask Claude to work across the whole set. In the project’s main prompt box, type a request like: *“Summarise the key ideas from all attached chats and the brief, and suggest three headline options.”* Claude will read every linked conversation and document, giving you a consolidated answer.  
💬 **Example:** Paste the sentence above and hit *Enter* – Claude will return a brief summary and headline suggestions.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the description:** A vague project name makes it hard to locate later. Always add a short purpose note.  
- **Adding unrelated chats:** Only pull in conversations that truly support the goal; unrelated threads clutter the view.  
- **Forgetting to upload files:** If you only add chats, any reference documents won’t be available for Claude to read.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can create a personal project for a home renovation, grouping design ideas, budget spreadsheets and chat advice in one place.  
- **For your business or work:** Teams can run a product launch project, keeping market research chats, marketing drafts and stakeholder feedback together, so no detail gets lost.  
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to open the Dashboard and click *New Project* – you’ll instantly see how tidy a single goal can become.

## Try it now
Spend the next two minutes opening Claude, hitting **Dashboard → New Project**, and naming a project after one current task (e.g., *“Weekly Report”*). Adding just that one project will give you a taste of how Claude Projects bring order to your work.
